title: rules
description: Rules constrain the space of legal actions in a game. They need not be written or fully explicit, but some constraint must exist or there is free play rather than a game; rules are what make choice meaningful.

constrainLegalActions.description: The defining condition: rules delimit what can be done, creating a space of meaningful choice rather than prescribing a predetermined result.

constitutive.description: Rules that bring the game into being — forbidding more efficient means in favor of the game's own (Suits 1978); accepting them is the lusory attitude.

explicit.description: Whether the rules are codified (a published rulebook) or held by negotiated consensus (children's games, folk variants).

houseRules.description: Local modifications adopted by a particular group — the game as played here, not the game in general.
